correctness.rationale: For sorted coordinates, each signed count-function summand is supported on one interval, and intervals of opposite signs are disjoint and index ordered. Thus the aggregate has at most s-1 sign changes. A self-contained confluent-exponential Chebyshev argument bounds all real Mellin-transform zeros with multiplicity by s-1. Equal total abundance forces M(0)=0, and a Shannon-order equality requires a double zero there. Thus at most s-2 positive-order ties. Exact integer sums 2362,-517776,16323602434 prove two crossings for the four-species witness; the universal bound makes them exactly two and transverse. The standalone verifier was executed successfully, and cannot replace the analytic argument.

originality.rationale: The 2012 primary source specifically discusses double-crossing and unlimited crossings across arbitrary support, but does not derive a minimum richness of four or a fixed-s upper bound. Patil–Taillie 1982 is a crossing theorem for special perturbations rather than an arbitrary pair. Full Gress–Rosenberg 2024 analyzes conditional magnitude bounds. Scientific-index and wider literature searches for power-majorization, Rényi profiles, s-2 crossing counts and the exact witness did not expose a covering theorem. A more general total-positivity theorem might imply the bound; originality has residual uncertainty.
residual_risks: An unindexed power-majorization or exponential-polynomial/total-positivity theorem may imply the intersection bound without using ecological terminology.
The complete Tóthmérész 1995 diversity-ordering article was not materially read; its abstract does not settle coverage.
An unpublished or not-yet-indexed analysis could already contain the minimal four-species construction.

value.rationale: Repeated reversals are directly meaningful for ecological comparison across Hill orders: Leinster–Cobbold 2012 records rare empirical double crossings and says arbitrarily many are possible with unrestricted richness. The precise smallest community size and a bound based on richness give an interpretable, structural sampling-scale restriction rather than a routine substituted formula or unmotivated numerical table. Both the supporting theorem and elementary exact witness address the same substantive question; empirical sampling uncertainty is not modeled.
